content.text:
I submitted index 11 (Ni 0.646, Sb 0.354) as the best composition. Its measured EQE was **0.522%**, the highest of the three I could measure. I used all 3 merit measurements and all 5 XRD scans.

**EQE results:**

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.66 (near the 1:2 NiSb₂O₆ ratio) | 0.015% |
| 16 | 0.51 | 0.464% |
| 11 | 0.35 | 0.522% |

EQE rose steadily as the film got richer in Ni.

**XRD results** (indices 5, 11, 16, 21, 26):
- The same NiSb₂O₆-type (trirutile) crystal structure is present in all five.
- **Sb-rich side:** a second, Sb-oxide phase starts to show at index 21 and is strong at index 26. This fits the very low EQE at index 21.
- **Ni-rich side:** indices 11 and 16 show only the trirutile phase. A weak NiO peak first appears at index 5.

**Why index 11:** it had the best measured EQE, and it sits in the single-phase range just before NiO starts to form.

**Caveat:** the true best composition may lie between indices 6 and 10, which I had no merit measurements left to test. The EQE was still rising toward the Ni-rich side, but more slowly (0.464% to 0.522%). I rejected index 5 because NiO is starting to appear there, but it was never measured.
